## Pass 1

Changes are listed as unit · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done. Units are numbered from 0, as in units.json. Every edit was made by script (scratchpad review1_edit.py for units.json, review1_lemmas.py for new-lemmas.txt). Each script asserts the old text before it replaces it. No glyph code, glyph order, q, rubric flag or restored flag was changed, and no word was joined or split. I found no majors: every verb form named in the notes matches the signs and the l / i, and the drafter's doubtful points are marked as doubtful.

- U17 · l, i · minor · The note calls dr·tn a sḏm·f used as a wish, which an imperative cannot be, since it carries ·tn. But l had "drive-out-you" and i had "Drive out all the evil…", which is an imperative · l → "may-drive-out-you"; i → "May you drive out all the evil that is mine, as you did for …".
- U26 · l, n · minor · The signs run ꜣḫw ipw 7 (w237–w239: χu, àpu, VII). l had "the-spirits · seven · these", and the note quoted the red words as "ꜣḫw 7 ipw". That order belongs to lines 86 and 102, not this line · l → "the-spirits · these · seven". The note now quotes "ir ẖrt ꜣḫw ipw 7" and says that here the numeral follows ipw, where in lines 86 and 102 it comes before it.
- U21, U26 · words[qbḥ-snw-f] glyphs 3–4 role, tr · minor · The pot W24 was coded comp "n" and the chick G43 phon "w". W24 writes nw, not n, and it supplies the w of snw; the chick then repeats that w. U8 and U29 code the pot as nw · W24 → phon "nw"; G43 → comp "w" (in both units).
- U33 · n · minor · wḏ had no form label, although l renders it "is-assigned(?)". st·i was given as 'my seat' with no word on the spelling. st 'seat' normally has the seat sign Q1 (as st·sn in U18 has). Bolt plus t is the usual spelling of the dependent pronoun st 'it', which is how Budge reads it · the note now names wḏ a passive sḏm with st·i as its subject. It gives Budge's alternative (st 'it', with the man as 'for me'). It also adds the strongest support for the reading wḏ: wḏ is regularly written with the cobra ḏ as its complement, and the snake joined to the stick may be that cobra drawn as the viper. The doubt is kept.
- U12 · n · minor · The passive reading of ḏdw was given as the only one. The w and the place of the word, straight after "the gods who are in the following of Horus", allow equally well the plural participle "who say", going with those gods · I added that alternative, and noted that neither reading is sure.
- U2 · l, n · style · l had "to · its-lord", but only nb is written · l → "to · (its)-lord", and the note says 'its' is supplied. The note on bgꜣ now adds that the word may be a writing of bꜣgi 'be weary, slack', with the ꜣ written after g. The doubt is kept.
- U15 · n · style · ddyw was called "the doubled participle of rdi" · → "the imperfective participle of rdi, with its doubled stem dd".
- new-lemmas.txt · bgꜣ, rmi, psg, nwy, spꜣ, sꜣm, irwd, BROADEN mr, sn, wꜥb · style · These entries described the signs of this occurrence ("written with the bird of bad things", "written with the weeping eye", "written with the house classifier"…). A glossary entry should not do that (the ruling of ani-017-b pass 1). psg also carried "the reading is not sure", which is a doubt about this passage, not about the lemma; the note on U4 keeps that doubt · the sign descriptions are removed. bgꜣ adds "perhaps a writing of bꜣgi". spꜣ → "a centipede god". irwd → "a building or place (?), not identified".
- new-lemmas.txt · BROADEN nn · style · The entry claimed "(later spelling)", a dating I cannot support (cf. ani-017-b pass 2, BROADEN m), and stated as fact the 'this is …' construction, which U8 marks as not sure · → "the demonstrative also written nnw; perhaps also standing first in a sentence without a verb, 'this is …' (?)".

### Refused findings
- U33, the reading of the group Z9 I9 V25 as wḏ (the drafter's first doubt): I weighed taking the viper as ·f of mꜣꜣ·tw·f, 'he is seen', with V25 alone as wḏ. That reading accounts for the viper. But the print sets viper and stick as one crossed group, and Budge leaves the whole group untransliterated, so the group stands together. The cobra-complement point (added above) makes wḏ the better guess. The unit is marked doubtful. Kept.
- U2, in·n·f + s split and the untranslated n: the bolt as the dependent pronoun s (the Eye) is the simplest reading. Joining s and n as sn 'them' does not suit a single Eye, and the n is said to have no clear place. Kept.
- U4, psg 'spit' against Budge's 'wash': the man with hand to mouth classifies what the mouth does, and psg 'spit' is an attested verb. The second s and the ꜣ are said not to be read. The misprint opening is fair, because only the doubled s is corrected; the doubt about the word as a whole is stated. The split of n·s from Budge's pesaḳ-nes is grammatical. Kept.
- U8, nnw nwy n pt: I considered nnw = Nun. But the same group (n, adze, pot, chick, without the water classifier) is the demonstrative in lines 80 and 86, and the note says the construction is not sure. Kept.
- U5, ḫpdt: the reading follows Budge, and the note says the classifiers cannot be identified. Kept.
- U29–U30, the seven spirit names: each is coded sign by sign, the unidentified signs are said to be so, and the meanings are hedged ('perhaps', 'not clear'). Budge's forms are in the notes and the glossary. Kept.
- U31, irwd·f shown as […]: no word irwd can be confirmed, and Budge's 'hall' rests on the house classifier alone. The glossary entry is now general (above). Kept.
- U32, ḏd wsir pw n rꜥ as 'the saying of Osiris to Ra': n marks the person spoken to, not the doer, so Budge's 'to Osiris by Ra' is rightly set aside, and the note says why. Kept.
- U25, the ir-clause without a predicate: the note gives both readings (the clause as the gloss itself, or a clause missing), and the i ends open to show what is written. Supplying 'it is (the evil) since …' would add words that are not there. Kept.
- Joins and splits: ṯs-pẖr (a fixed phrase, 'vice versa'), ir·n (a sḏm·n·f), m-sꜣ (the compound preposition, joined across Budge's numeral, both halves red), nḏ-ḥr (as in ani-017-b), st·i (the alternative is now in the note); the splits in·n·f + s, psg + n·s and m·tn + wi. Each is grammatical, and each note says that Budge's groups were changed. q is re-indexed correctly in all eleven regrouped words. Kept.
- Corrections psꜣgs → psg and dwꜣ-mwt-r → dwꜣ-mwt-f: in the second, the sense allows only the god's name (the same four sons are named three times), so the misprint rule fits exactly. On psg, see above. Kept.
- U1 / U9 irt with lemma irt and D4 log, where ani-017-b codes irt under ir with D4 phon: irt is a known key and both codings are defensible. Normalising the published parts is not this part's business. Kept.
- U2, U17 / U18, U32 lemma n vs ny: the preposition and negation are keyed n, and the genitive ny, throughout, as in the published parts. Kept.
- U18, U32 mi with the arm (D36) and two strokes coded phon ꜥ / y, not read: this is identical to ani-125-address, and the known gloss of mi describes this spelling. Kept.
- U24 T14 in nsrt, U26 Y1 in ẖry-bꜣq-f, U34 the lone × before ṯꜣfy, all coded det: these are unidentified or surplus signs with no value to give, and the notes say they are not read. Kept.
- U3, wnn left untranslated: the note explains it, and l shows "(wnn)". Kept.
- `say`: every form follows the rule or the published parts (Sobek as in ani-125-address; the four sons of Horus and the seven names are new and are built by rule; "Webes", "wedja", "wenen" follow the published practice of an e after initial w). Kept.
- Budge-isms and remembered wording: none in l / i. "triumphant", "homage", "avenger", "beatified", "decreed", "Amentet", "the two Tchafi" and "defect" appear only in the notes, as Budge's renderings. "Hail to you", "true of voice", "the West", "lords of Maat" and "tribunal" are the published parts' wording. Kept.

Re-check after editing: units.json parses and keeps its formatting (indent 1, ensure_ascii off, no trailing newline). The 1216 sign codes, in order, equal the established w0..w310. There are 309 words: five joins and three splits, and q in all eleven regrouped words checked against the established q. Rubric flags match the established file sign for sign. The restored flags are unchanged: only N35 and Z2 of st·sn in U18, where Budge's brackets stand, and the note says they are restored. Every unit with red words says so. Morph coverage is exact in every word. Every det has an empty tr. Every comp repeats a consonant of its word's reading; the two exceptions are I10 ḏ in ind, the published coding, and the bolt z in sꜣmt, s written as z. Every Z9 at a horned viper has the viper's role and an empty tr. Every morph lemma is a key of known-lemmas.json or an entry of new-lemmas.txt. No new entry collides with a known key, every BROADEN key exists and is used, and every new entry is used. The longest note is 1391 characters.
